Around that time the church in Philippi sent Epaphroditus to bring Paul a gift. Epaphroditus fell ill and nearly died, but he recovered. Paul sent him back to Philippi with a letter.

Paul wrote in the letter, “What has happened to me has actually helped the gospel spread. The whole imperial guard has come to know that I am in chains for Christ. For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain. Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: rejoice.” A man in chains was sending joy to the church in Philippi.

words.text: Brothers, I want you to know that what has happened to me has actually helped the gospel spread.
For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: rejoice.
Paul proclaimed the kingdom of God very boldly and without hindrance, and he taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

a39.note: Philippians is a letter Paul wrote while in prison. Here we follow the old view that he wrote it in his rented house in Rome. Some scholars think he wrote it while imprisoned in Ephesus or Caesarea.
a39.reflect: Am I using my circumstances as an excuse to put off what I could do today?

quiz.q: Who brought the gift from the church in Philippi to Paul in Rome and then fell ill?
quiz.explain: Paul writes that he received what the Philippians sent through Epaphroditus, and that Epaphroditus was ill and nearly died, but God had mercy on him (Phil 4:18; 2:25–27).

a40.title: A Letter for Onesimus
a40.subtitle: From useless to useful
story: A man named Onesimus came to Paul, who was a prisoner in Rome. He was a slave from the house of Philemon, of the church in Colossae, and he had been away from his master for some time. Through Paul in his chains, Onesimus came to faith. Paul wanted to keep him by his side, but he decided not to do anything without Philemon's consent. So he sent Onesimus back to his master with a short letter.

Paul wrote to Philemon, “Onesimus was once useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me. Welcome him now not as a slave but as a dear brother. If he owes you anything, charge it to me. I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand. I will pay it back.”

Paul also wrote letters to the churches in Colossae and Ephesus. In Colossians he wrote that in Christ there is no slave or free, and in Ephesians he wrote that we are saved by grace through faith. The letters were carried by Tychicus, a coworker from Asia. Onesimus went with him to Colossae. Paul introduced Onesimus to the church in Colossae like this: “Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, who is one of you.”

words.text: Welcome him now not as a slave, but as more than a slave: a dear brother.
If he has wronged you or owes you anything, charge it to me. I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand. I will pay it back.
You have been saved by grace through faith. This is not from yourselves; it is the gift of God.
Tychicus will tell you all my news. Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, is coming with him.

a40.note: The name Onesimus means “useful” in Greek. Paul made a play on that name. Here we follow the old view that these three letters were written in Rome, though some think they were written in Ephesus.
a40.reflect: Am I keeping someone tied to their past wrongs?

quiz.q: Who went to Colossae with Onesimus and brought news of Paul?
quiz.explain: Paul wrote that Tychicus would tell them everything about him, and that he was sending Onesimus with him (Col 4:7–9). The letter to the Ephesians was also sent with Tychicus (Eph 6:21–22).

a41.title: Titus Left Behind on Crete
a41.subtitle: Titus on an island, Timothy in a city
story: The book of Acts ends in the rented house in Rome, but the letters to Timothy and Titus show Paul traveling freely again. As Paul left for Macedonia, he told young Timothy to stay in Ephesus. He was to correct people who taught a different doctrine or got lost in endless family records.

Some time later Paul sent Timothy a letter. Paul wrote, “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I am the worst of them. Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young. Be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity.”

Paul left Titus on the island of Crete. Paul wrote to Titus, “I left you in Crete to set right what was still unfinished and to appoint elders in every town.” At the end of the letter he told Titus to hurry to Nicopolis when he sent Artemas or Tychicus, because he had decided to spend the winter there. He also asked Titus to send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, who had taught in Corinth, on their way with everything they needed.

words.text: Here is a saying you can trust, worthy of everyone's welcome: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. And I am the worst of them.
Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young. Be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity.
I left you in Crete to set right what was still unfinished and to appoint elders in every town, as I told you.

a41.note: Acts says nothing about Paul working on Crete. So many scholars think Paul was released after his two years in Rome and traveled again. Nicopolis is thought to be a city on the northwest coast of Greece.
a41.reflect: Am I raising up people of faith who can carry on the work I have been given?

quiz.q: Why did Paul leave Titus on Crete?
options: To set right what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town
To find a ship bound for Rome
To collect a gift for the church in Jerusalem
quiz.explain: Paul wrote to Titus that he had left him in Crete to set right what was lacking and to appoint elders in every town (Titus 1:5).

a42.title: The Good Fight Fought to the End
a42.subtitle: Looking toward the crown of righteousness
story: When he wrote his last letter, Paul was in chains in Rome. Paul wrote to Timothy, “My life is already being poured out like wine on the altar, and the time of my departure is near. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Now the crown of righteousness is waiting for me. On that day the Lord will give it to me, and not only to me but to all who long for his coming.”

He was lonely. Demas had loved this world and gone off to Thessalonica. Crescens had gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia. Only Luke was with Paul. Paul wrote, “Bring Mark with you. He is a help to me in my work.” It was the same Mark over whom Paul and Barnabas had parted ways. Paul also asked him to bring the cloak he had left in Troas, and the books, especially the parchments.

Paul wrote, “At my first defense in court, no one stood by me. Everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them. But the Lord stood beside me and gave me strength. Through me he made sure the message was fully proclaimed, so that all the Gentiles might hear it.” Paul asked once more: “Do your best to come before winter.”

words.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
Now the crown of righteousness is waiting for me. The Lord, the righteous Judge, will give it to me on that day.
Everyone deserted me, but the Lord stood beside me and gave me strength.
Do your best to come before winter.

a42.note: Second Timothy is thought to be the last of Paul's letters. The account of Paul's martyrdom in Rome is an old tradition from outside the Bible, so this journey closes the story with Paul's own confession.
a42.core: Paul's last hope was not pride in what he had achieved. It was the crown of righteousness that the Lord, the righteous Judge, would give him (2 Tim 4:7–8).
a42.reflect: At the end of my life, will I be able to say that the Lord was with me?

quiz.q: Whom did Paul ask Timothy to bring, saying he was a help in his work?
quiz.explain: Paul wrote, “Bring Mark with you, for he is useful to me in my work” (2 Tim 4:11). Demas had left because he loved the world, and Tychicus had been sent to Ephesus (2 Tim 4:10, 12).

gal.name: Galatians
gal.why: After Paul left, some people came to the churches of Galatia and taught that Gentile believers had to be circumcised and keep the law to be saved. When the believers were shaken by this and began turning to a different gospel, Paul was shocked and grieved, and he wrote this letter.
gal.heart: A person is made right with God not by keeping the law but by faith in Christ, and in that faith we are truly free.
verses: I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
Christ has set us free so that we may be free. So stand firm, and do not put on the yoke of slavery again.
The fruit the Spirit produces is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
gal.view: Some think it was written during the third journey, after the Jerusalem council, in Ephesus or Macedonia, around AD 53–57.

1th.name: 1 Thessalonians
1th.why: Paul had to leave Thessalonica in a hurry because of persecution. Worried, he sent Timothy, and when Timothy came back with news of their faith and love, Paul was glad and wrote this letter. They were grieving because they did not know what would happen to believers who had already died, so he also gave them that hope.
1th.heart: To a church that kept the faith in suffering, Paul gives encouragement to live holy lives while hoping for the day the Lord comes again.
verses: Because we cared for you so deeply, we were glad to share with you not only the gospel of God but our very lives, because you had become so dear to us.
Do not grieve like people who have no hope. If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, then God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep in Jesus.
Always be joyful. Never stop praying. Give thanks in everything. This is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.

2th.name: 2 Thessalonians
2th.why: The believers in Thessalonica were shaken by talk that the day of the Lord had already come, and some stopped working and lived idly. Paul wrote this letter to tell them what must happen before that day comes, and to urge them to live quietly and do their own work.
2th.heart: Do not be shaken about the day the Lord will come. Hold firmly to the teaching you received, and live today faithfully.
verses: The Lord is faithful. He will make you strong and guard you from the evil one.
Even when we were with you, we told you this: anyone who will not work should not eat.
May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. May the Lord be with you all.

1co.name: 1 Corinthians
1co.why: While Paul was in Ephesus, people from Chloe's household told him that the church in Corinth had split into groups. The Corinthians also sent him a letter asking about things like marriage and food offered to idols. Paul wrote this letter, answering these matters one by one.
1co.heart: To a divided, quarreling church, Paul says: become one body in the gospel of the cross and in love.
verses: The message of the cross sounds foolish to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
Love is patient and kind. Love does not envy, does not boast, is not proud. It is not rude, does not seek its own way, is not easily angered, and does not keep a record of wrongs.
Christ died for our sins as the Scriptures said, he was buried, and he was raised on the third day as the Scriptures said.

2co.name: 2 Corinthians
2co.to: The church in Corinth and all the believers in Achaia
2co.why: After sending the church in Corinth a letter written with tears, Paul waited anxiously. When he met Titus in Macedonia and heard the good news that the believers were sorry, Paul wrote this letter to share his comfort, to answer those who doubted his calling as an apostle, and to ask them to get ready their gift for the believers in Jerusalem.
2co.heart: A treasure held in people as weak as clay jars: God's power is made perfect in weakness.
verses: We have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that this great power comes from God and not from us.
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has gone. Look, the new has come.
The Lord said to me, “My grace is enough for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” So I will boast all the more gladly about my weakness, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.

rom.name: Romans
rom.carrier: Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchreae
rom.why: Paul had long wanted to go to Rome. He planned to deliver the gift collected by the believers in Macedonia and Achaia to Jerusalem, and then go on to Spain by way of Rome. So he sent this letter to the believers in Rome, whom he had never met, carefully laying out the gospel he preached.
rom.heart: Jews and Gentiles alike are all under sin, but anyone who believes in Jesus Christ is made right before God.
verses: I am not ashamed of the gospel. It is the power of God that saves everyone who believes, first the Jew and then the Greek.
While we were still sinners, Christ died for us. In this way God showed his love for us.
Neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither things present nor things to come, nothing at all can separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

php.name: Philippians
php.why: The church in Philippi sent Epaphroditus with a gift for Paul in prison. Epaphroditus became so ill at Paul's side that he nearly died, but he recovered. Paul sent him back with this letter to say thank you, and to urge them to be of one mind and to rejoice in the Lord.
php.heart: Even in chains we can rejoice in Christ, and in every situation he is our strength.
verses: For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Do not worry about anything. In everything, pray, and with thanksgiving tell God what you need. Then the peace of God, which is beyond all human understanding, will guard your hearts.
I can do all things through him who gives me strength.
php.view: Some think it was written while Paul was imprisoned in Ephesus or Caesarea.

phm.name: Philemon
phm.to: Philemon of Colossae and the church that meets in his house
phm.why: Onesimus, a slave who had left Philemon, met Paul in prison and became a believer. Paul sent Onesimus back to his master Philemon with this short letter, asking him to welcome Onesimus now not as a slave but as a dear brother.
phm.heart: The gospel turns even master and slave into brothers.
verses: Onesimus was once useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.
Welcome him now not as a slave, but as more than a slave: a dear brother.
If he has wronged you or owes you anything, charge it to me.
phm.view: Some think it was written while Paul was imprisoned in Ephesus.

col.name: Colossians
col.why: Epaphras, who had brought the gospel to Colossae, told Paul news of the church. Teachings had crept in there about human philosophy, rules about food, and the worship of angels. Paul wrote this letter to remind them that Christ alone is enough.
col.heart: All the fullness of God is in Christ, who was before all creation, so in him we lack nothing.
verses: He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.
In Christ all the fullness of God lives in bodily form, and in him you too have been made full.
Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as for the Lord and not for people.
col.view: Some think it was written while Paul was imprisoned in Ephesus or Caesarea.

eph.name: Ephesians
eph.why: This letter was not written to settle a quarrel. Paul wrote it to show how rich the grace is that God has given in Christ, how God has joined Jews and Gentiles into one body, and to urge them to live in a way worthy of that calling.
eph.heart: Those saved by grace have become one body in Christ, so live as one, in a way worthy of that calling.
verses: You have been saved by grace, through faith. This is not from yourselves; it is the gift of God. It is not from works, so no one can boast.
Always be humble and gentle. Be patient and bear with one another in love. Work hard to keep the unity the Spirit gives, bound together by peace.
Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor God gives you, so that you can stand against the devil's schemes.
eph.view: Some think it was written while Paul was imprisoned in Ephesus or Caesarea. Some old manuscripts leave out the words “in Ephesus,” so some see it as a letter passed around among several churches.

1ti.name: 1 Timothy
1ti.why: On his way to Macedonia, Paul left Timothy in Ephesus and gave him the task of stopping those who taught a different doctrine. Paul wrote this letter to show how people should live in the church, the household of God, and what kind of people should be chosen as overseers and deacons.
1ti.heart: To a young worker: guard the true teaching and fight the good fight of faith.
verses: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. This saying can be trusted and deserves to be welcomed by everyone. And I am the worst of sinners.
Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young. Instead, be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called.
1ti.view: The letter does not say where it was written. Because Paul says he left Timothy behind when he went to Macedonia (1 Tim 1:3), it is placed in Macedonia, and the map marks Philippi in Macedonia. Since it comes after the end of Acts, some date it differently.

tit.name: Titus
tit.why: Paul left Titus on Crete and gave him the task of setting right what was unfinished and appointing elders in every town. There were people there deceiving others with empty talk. In this letter Paul told Titus what kind of people to appoint as elders and how the believers should devote themselves to doing good.
tit.heart: The grace of God that saved us shapes us into people eager to do good.
verses: The grace of God that brings salvation to all people has appeared. It teaches us to turn away from ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in this world.
God saved us not because of anything right we had done, but because of his mercy. The Holy Spirit washed us, gave us new birth, and made us new.
This saying can be trusted. Speak about these things with confidence, so that those who believe in God will be careful to devote themselves to doing good.
tit.view: The letter does not say where it was written. Since Paul planned to spend the winter in Nicopolis (Titus 3:12), it is thought he wrote it on the way from Macedonia to Nicopolis. The map marks Philippi in Macedonia. Some date it differently.

2ti.name: 2 Timothy
2ti.why: Imprisoned again in Rome, Paul knew the time of his death was near. Only Luke was still with him. Paul asked Timothy, his dear son, to hurry and come before winter and to bring the cloak and books he had left behind. He left his last charge: guard the gospel and endure hardship.
2ti.heart: An old apostle who has run to the end hands the baton of the gospel to the next generation.
verses: The spirit God has given us is not a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
All Scripture is breathed out by God. It is useful for teaching, for showing what is wrong, for correcting, and for training in right living.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Now the crown of righteousness is waiting for me.
